description: Labelled questions over five public documents, for measuring retrieval accuracy and abstention. Answerable questions carry the page range where the answer lives, taken from the document’s own outline. Unanswerable ones are covered by no document in the corpus.

unanswerable.question: In MySQL 8, how large should I set innodb_buffer_pool_size on a write-heavy server with 64 GB of RAM?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: the PostgreSQL 17 manual documents shared_buffers, work_mem and checkpoint tuning for write-heavy loads, and OSTEP discusses buffer caches, but neither documents MySQL or InnoDB. No document in the corpus describes any MySQL variable. The nearest passage (PostgreSQL 'Resource Consumption') is the least-bad-passage trap, not an answer.

unanswerable.question: Which Redis maxmemory-policy should I pick for a cache that also holds a job queue I cannot afford to drop?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: OSTEP covers LRU/clock replacement policies and PostgreSQL covers buffer eviction, so 'eviction policy' matches strongly, but Redis, maxmemory-policy and allkeys-lru appear in none of the five documents. C++, NIST 800-53 and the Spanish penal code are unrelated.

unanswerable.question: How do I run several Python coroutines concurrently with asyncio.gather and cancel the rest when one exceeds its timeout?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: N4950 specifies C++ coroutines (co_await, promise types) and OSTEP covers concurrency and cancellation-like synchronization, so 'coroutines' and 'concurrently' both hit, but Python and asyncio are absent from the entire corpus.

unanswerable.question: Why does Rust's borrow checker reject handing an &mut reference to a spawned thread unless the type is Send?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: N4950 defines C++'s data-race and memory model and OSTEP explains shared-memory threading hazards, so the underlying concept is adjacent, but Rust, borrow checking, lifetimes and the Send/Sync traits are documented nowhere in the five documents.

unanswerable.question: When is ZGC a better choice than G1 for a JVM service with a 200 GB heap and a 10 ms pause budget?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: OSTEP covers memory management, free-space allocation and paging, and C++23 (N4950) removed even its garbage-collection support API, so 'heap' and 'collector' match loosely. No document covers the JVM or any specific garbage collector implementation.

unanswerable.question: What does a least-privilege AWS IAM policy look like for an S3 bucket that only receives audit logs and is never read back?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: NIST SP 800-53r5 defines AC-6 (Least Privilege) and the whole AU audit-logging family, so the terms 'least privilege' and 'audit log' match hard, but 800-53 states control requirements, not AWS IAM JSON policies or S3 configuration. No AWS documentation exists in the corpus.

unanswerable.question: GDPR Article 33 gives 72 hours to notify a breach - does that clock start at detection or at confirmation of the incident?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: NIST SP 800-53r5 has IR-6 incident reporting and the PT privacy family, with organization-defined reporting timeframes, so 'breach notification' matches. The GDPR text and its 72-hour rule are not in 800-53r5, and the Spanish document is the criminal code, not data-protection regulation.

unanswerable.question: Which TLS 1.3 cipher suites should I put in my nginx ssl_ciphers directive to pass a PCI DSS scan?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: NIST SP 800-53r5 requires cryptographic protection (SC-8, SC-13) and PostgreSQL documents ssl settings for the server, but no document lists TLS 1.3 cipher suites, contains nginx directives, or covers PCI DSS requirements.

unanswerable.question: For running a replicated database on Kubernetes, is a StatefulSet with a headless service better than a Deployment with a PersistentVolumeClaim?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: The PostgreSQL 17 manual covers streaming and logical replication in depth, which will pull strong matches on 'replicated database', but Kubernetes, StatefulSets, Deployments and PVCs appear in none of the five documents.

unanswerable.question: How do I set up a GitHub Actions matrix build that compiles my project against GCC 13, Clang 17 and MSVC 19.4?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: N4950 defines the C++ language and library but says nothing about specific toolchains, build systems or CI services; GitHub Actions and compiler vendor releases are absent from all five documents.

unanswerable.question: What chunk size and overlap should I use when embedding a large PDF manual for vector search?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: A plausible question for a document assistant, but the corpus is the subject matter (a DB manual, a language standard, a controls catalog, a penal code, an OS textbook), not documentation about retrieval pipelines. The PostgreSQL 17 core manual has no pgvector or embeddings chapter.

unanswerable.question: What PromQL alerting rule catches a slow memory leak before the kernel OOM-killer terminates the process?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Vocabulary trap: OSTEP explains virtual memory, resident set size and swapping, and C++ covers allocation and leaks conceptually, so 'memory leak' matches. Prometheus, PromQL and alerting rules are not documented anywhere in the corpus.

unanswerable.question: ¿Cuántos días de salario por año trabajado corresponden como indemnización por despido improcedente según el Estatuto de los Trabajadores?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Trampa de vocabulario en español: el Código Penal tipifica los delitos contra los derechos de los trabajadores (arts. 311 y ss.), por lo que 'trabajadores' coincide con fuerza, pero el Estatuto de los Trabajadores y las indemnizaciones por despido son derecho laboral y no figuran en ninguno de los cinco documentos.

unanswerable.question: ¿Qué plazo concede la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Civil para contestar a la demanda en un juicio ordinario y cómo se computa?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Trampa de vocabulario en español: el Código Penal consolidado es derecho sustantivo (delitos, penas, prescripción) y no contiene normas procesales; los plazos de la LEC, la demanda y el juicio ordinario no aparecen en el corpus. Los otros cuatro documentos son técnicos y en inglés.

unanswerable.question: ¿Cómo configuro un replica set de MongoDB con miembros en varias regiones y qué write concern debería usar?
unanswerable.why_uncovered: Doble trampa: está en español (como el Código Penal, que no trata de bases de datos) y usa vocabulario de replicación que coincide con los capítulos de replicación en streaming y lógica del manual de PostgreSQL 17. MongoDB, los replica sets y el write concern no aparecen en ningún documento del corpus.
